pages.text: "Hey, move, slowpoke!" Pipo shouted while rolling his wooden ball in the yard. Mrs. Goose and her goslings stood in the middle. The ball rolled to her feet and stopped.
Long-necked Mrs. Goose repeated exactly, "Hey, move, slowpoke!" Then she tucked the ball under a wing. Pipo wanted it back. "My ball..."
"Give it back, fool!" Pipo stamped. She stretched her neck and repeated, "Give it back, fool!" The ball stayed under her wing. His eyes filled with tears.
Mom came out of the kitchen and sat beside him. "Pipo, how does it feel if someone calls you a fool?" He thought carefully. "Mmm... really upsetting."
Mom whispered, "Mrs. Goose is a mirror. Your words come right back. Kind words come back kindly!" His eyes sparkled. "Oh, that is why the ball did not come back either!"
Pipo practiced shaping new words: instead of "Move," "May I pass?" Instead of "Give it back," "Please." Mom nodded beside him.
Pipo went before Mrs. Goose. "I am sorry. May I have the ball, please?" She stretched her neck and smiled back. "Yes, Pipo. Here it is." Kind words come back kindly!
With a wingtip, she rolled the ball to him. He caught it with both hands, then put it down and crouched, hands at his chest.

The goslings pushed the ball over. Spreading both arms, Pipo spoke first. "Thank you! One, think first! Two, change to kind words! Three, thank you and sorry!" Behind, Mrs. Goose watched with her long neck stretched.
Pipo laid both hands on her wing and nestled close. "Let us play together tomorrow too!" Kind words returned as kind words. Side by side, they called, "Kind words come back kindly!"
